intended_object: The canonical bijection Hom_{Pro(FinSet)}(Q,R) ≅ C(|Q|,|R|) between morphisms of pro-finite sets (dual ind-objects of finite sets) and continuous maps between their profinite realizations (limits of their presentations), i.e. the hom-action of the fully faithful realization functor Pro(FinSet) → Profinite. Inferred from the docstring, module doc, and its use in `indDualRealizationFullyFaithful`.
explanation: The definition composes (1) transport along the chosen Ind-presentation isomorphisms Q ≅ finiteDiagramIndDual(diagram of Q) and similarly for R, with (2) the library's bijection between dual-ind morphisms of specified cofiltered finite-set diagrams and continuous maps between their Profinite limits, using `Profinite.limitCone`. Its forward map is definitionally `indDualRealization.map f` (lemma `indDualRealizationHomEquiv_apply` is `rfl`). So it is exactly the hom-set bijection of the realization functor, which is a bijection because it is an `Equiv`. The file uses it to build `indDualRealizationFullyFaithful`, matching the docstring. Using `FintypeCat.Skeleton` instead of `FintypeCat` is harmless up to equivalence, and working in one universe matches the standard size convention for Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite. The construction is about profinite spaces and pro-finite sets by nature, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has `Ind` but no pro-category of finite sets and no equivalence between it and `Profinite`, so there is no counterpart.
